page.title: Webinar Production Agency Selection Guide
page.description: Learn what a webinar production agency delivers, typical costs, timelines, staffing models, and how to evaluate partners before you sign.
page.h1: How do you choose the right webinar production partner?
page.definition: A webinar production agency is a service team that plans, rehearses, and runs live virtual events on your chosen platform, handling run of show, speaker prep, backup streams, and edited recordings.
page.quick_answer: Pick an agency that owns the run of show, provides a named producer, rehearses on your platform days before go-live, and delivers edited clips within 48 hours.

sections.h2: What does a webinar production agency deliver?

blocks.p: A production partner supplies the crew, run of show, speaker brief and rehearsal, branded slide template and lower thirds, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, edited recording and clips.

ul: Run of show document with cues and timings
Speaker brief and rehearsal on the real platform
Branded slide template and lower thirds
Edited recording and short clips for reuse

sections.h2: How much does webinar production cost?

blocks.p: Pricing follows three cost models: per-host licences sized by attendee capacity (Zoom Webinars), self-serve monthly plans (StreamYard, Livestorm), and annual contracts quoted by sales (ON24, Cvent, Bizzabo, Goldcast).

head: Engagement type
Published range
rows: Executive summits, online conferences and hybrid productions

sections.h2: What timeline should I plan for a webinar?

blocks.p: Allow two to three weeks from brief to live; a repeat format can move faster. Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final.

ol: Run of show draft and speaker confirmation
Branded assets and slide template delivery
Full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before
Technical check 60 minutes before going live
Replay and clips delivered within 24 to 48 hours

sections.h2: Who owns each workstream during production?

blocks.p: Eight workstreams, each with one owner, keep the show on track from intake through reporting.

sections.h2: How do I evaluate an agency's process before hiring?

blocks.p: Ask for evidence of a documented workflow with named owners, approval gates, and tool choices that match your stack.

ul: Written run of show template shared before kickoff
Rehearsal scheduled on your platform, not a test room
Backup stream configured and tested before live
Edited recording and clips delivered within 48 hours
Post-event report with attendance, engagement, and lead data
Clear escalation path for technical issues during the show

faq.q: What is the difference between platform and production?
faq.a: The platform is software such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24 or StreamYard; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show and backup stream. Someone still has to own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready.

faq.q: How many people does a simple webinar need versus a summit?
faq.a: One producer can run a simple webinar; summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. Staffing scales with complexity and risk.

faq.q: When should I schedule the rehearsal and technical check?
faq.a: One full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before, and a technical check 60 minutes before going live. This catches audio, video, and platform permission issues early.

faq.q: How fast should the replay and clips be delivered?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours, while attendees still remember the event. Edited clips for social and nurture sequences should arrive in the same window.
